risks.title: Persistent Energy Shock and Geopolitical Instability
risks.summary: Ongoing conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, are driving sharp increases in energy prices, fueling inflation, and creating uncertainty. This shock is not over and poses a significant risk to global growth and stability.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East, oil price fluctuations, and the replenishment of strategic reserves.
sources: IMF (World Economic Outlook, September 02 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 12 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects, June 2026)
Federal Reserve (Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, August 19 2026)
Federal Reserve (FOMC statement, July 29 2026)

risks.title: Elevated Public Debt and Rising Debt Servicing Costs
risks.summary: Global public debt has reached near-record levels, exceeding post-WWII highs. Rising debt servicing costs are constraining government spending, particularly in developing economies, threatening long-term growth and debt sustainability.
risks.watch_for: Government debt-to-GDP ratios, interest rate trends, and fiscal consolidation plans.
sources: IMF (World Economic Outlook, September 02 2026)
IMF (Statement at the Conclusion of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting, September 01 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, February 11 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Outlook for the Budget and the Economy, February 01 2026)

risks.title: Stalled Disinflation and Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: While global inflation is expected to fall, US inflation is predicted to return to target more gradually. New inflationary impulses from AI capex spillovers and energy costs are emerging, complicating monetary policy.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings, wage growth, and energy price trends.
sources: IMF (World Economic Outlook, September 02 2026)

risks.title: Uncertainty over AI's Economic and Financial Effects
risks.summary: The rapid build-out of artificial intelligence is a key driver of growth, but uncertainty remains about its full economic and financial implications, including potential impacts on productivity, market valuations, and energy demand.
risks.watch_for: AI investment trends, productivity growth data, and AI-related corporate earnings.
sources: IMF (World Economic Outlook, September 02 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (August 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, August 17 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Narrowing Drivers of US Economic Expansion
risks.summary: The US expansion is increasingly reliant on a narrow set of drivers, primarily tech investment and wealth-driven consumer spending. Any disruption to these key areas could pose a significant downside risk to overall growth.
risks.watch_for: Disruptions to the AI investment thesis, changes in equity market valuations, and consumer spending patterns.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (August 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, August 17 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20 2026)

risks.title: Weak Real Income Growth and Consumer Spending Headwinds
risks.summary: Despite some support from wealth effects and tax refunds, real income growth is soft, and consumer spending faces headwinds from elevated prices and the depletion of fiscal support, potentially moderating overall economic expansion.
risks.watch_for: Real personal income growth, consumer spending data, and the impact of fading fiscal stimulus.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (August 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, August 17 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (June 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, June 16 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20 2026)
KPMG (December 11 2025)

risks.title: Widening Global Economic Imbalances
risks.summary: Global economic imbalances have widened significantly, reaching their largest increase in a decade. These imbalances can signal uneven growth patterns, macro-financial vulnerabilities, and potentially lead to trade tensions and economic fragmentation.
risks.watch_for: Current account balances of major economies and trade policy developments.
sources: IMF (Statement at the Conclusion of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors Meeting, September 01 2026)
IMF (World Economic Outlook, September 02 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Weakness and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While some reports indicate labor market stabilization, others flag ongoing weakness and concerns about affordability for consumers, particularly regarding prices for essentials like healthcare and energy.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate trends, wage growth, and consumer price indices for key goods and services.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
KPMG (January 12 2026)
KPMG (June 10 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus that the global economy is experiencing a period of resilient but uncertain growth, with AI investment being a significant driver. However, persistent risks from energy shocks, elevated public debt, and stalled disinflation are a major concern across institutions. While some foresee a moderation in inflation, others highlight ongoing pressures, particularly in the US.
themes: Inflationary Pressures and Monetary Policy Dilemmas
Global Economic Imbalances and Trade Policy
